from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.wait(3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Strategy: Frequency vs. Positional Probability", [
            "Letter frequency determines word strength.", 
            "We map frequency across all slots.", 
            "This calculates a word's weighted score."
        ])
        
        # --- Preparation ---
        freq_text = Text("Frequency: E=12%, Z=0.1%", color="#FFFFFF")
        pos_grid = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.8) for _ in range(5)]).arrange(RIGHT)
        score_calc = MathTex(r"Score = \sum P(char, slot)", color="#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(freq_text, "B2", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Write(freq_text))
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(pos_grid, "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(pos_grid))
        self.play(freq_text.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.place_at_grid(score_calc, "F3", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(score_calc))
        self.play(Indicate(pos_grid))
        self.wait(3)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Algorithmic Walkthrough: The Minimax Algorithm", [
            "Minimax minimizes the maximum remaining possibilities.",
            "It guarantees worst-case performance bounds.",
            "Decision trees visualize this branching process."
        ])
        
        # --- Visualization Setup ---
        root = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(root, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        title_tag = Text("Minimax Algorithm", font_size=32, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(title_tag, 'A3')
        self.play(Write(title_tag), Create(root))
        self.wait(3) # B029: Increase wait for conceptual intro

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Branching nodes
        nodes = VGroup()
        for i in range(3):
            n = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.5)
            nodes.add(n)
        
        self.place_at_grid(nodes[0], 'D2')
        self.place_at_grid(nodes[1], 'D3')
        self.place_at_grid(nodes[2], 'D4')
        
        lines = VGroup(*[Line(root.get_center(), n.get_center(), stroke_width=2) for n in nodes])
        self.play(Create(lines), Create(nodes))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        terminal = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(terminal, 'E3')
        target = Dot(color="#00FF00").move_to(terminal.get_center()) # B007: Terminal anchor
        
        self.play(Create(terminal), FadeIn(target))
        
        # Propagation animation (Upward)
        val_text = Text("Value", font_size=16, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(val_text, 'F3')
        self.play(Write(val_text))
        self.play(val_text.animate.move_to(root.get_center()), run_time=2) # B033: Animator/Updater-like movement
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Practical Application & Summary", ["Use a high-entropy starting word.", "Filter candidates based on feedback.", "Strategy leads to reliable wins."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        flowchart = VGroup(

        self.play(FadeOut(app_text), FadeOut(flowchart))

outline.topic: Optimal Wordle Strategy: An Algorithmic Approach
outline.target_audience: University students with basic probability/computer science interest

sections.title: The Game Mechanics: Information Theory Basics
sections.content: Introduce Wordle as a 'Search' problem. Explain that each guess is not just a word, but a query to reduce the search space (the set of remaining possible words).
sections.example: Visual: A large circle (2,315 possible answers) splits into smaller slices based on the feedback of your first guess (e.g., 'CRANE').

sections.title: Prerequisite: Entropy and Information Gain
sections.content: Define Entropy (H) as the measure of uncertainty. An optimal first word is one that provides the maximum expected information (partitions the remaining word set most evenly).
sections.example: Graphical chart: Comparing 'XYZZA' (low info, leaves 500 options) vs 'CRANE' (high info, leaves 60 options on average).

sections.title: The Strategy: Frequency vs. Positional Probability
sections.content: Analyze why letters like E, A, R, I, O, T are statistically superior. We map letter frequency across all 5 slots to calculate a 'Weighted Score' for any candidate word.
sections.example: A heatmap overlay on a QWERTY keyboard showing 'E' glowing bright red, 'Z' in dark blue; a robot character 'WordleBot' calculates a score for 'ARISE'.

sections.title: Algorithmic Walkthrough: The Minimax Algorithm
sections.content: Explain the Minimax strategy: Minimizing the maximum possible number of remaining words after a guess. This guarantees a worst-case performance.
sections.example: A decision tree animation: Root node (guess) branches out into feedback patterns (e.g., G-Y-B-B-B), leading to smaller candidate pools.

sections.title: Practical Application & Summary
sections.content: Conclude with the 'Golden Rule': Use a high-entropy opener (CRANE, SLATE, or ADIEU), then pivot to a 'filter' word if the first guess is ambiguous.
sections.example: A cat character playing the game: It picks 'SLATE', sees a green 'S', and instantly filters its internal database from 2,315 down to 42 options.
